title: Two squares that look completely different can be the exact same grey
body: In Edward Adelson’s 1995 checker shadow illusion, a square in the light looks dark and a square in a cylinder’s shadow looks light, yet on the page they are exactly the same shade. Your visual system isn’t measuring raw brightness: it estimates the true colour of surfaces by compensating for lighting and shadows. That usually helps you see the world accurately, but here it makes identical patches look strikingly different.
